material_systems.name: Interior Adhesion Primer
material_systems.description: Water-based adhesion promoter for previously painted interior stair components. Bonds to glossy, chalky, or oil-based existing coatings without full mechanical sanding. Primary RP primer for sound-to-peeling conditions. Stair components historically received oil-based paint (semi-gloss/gloss default sheen for durability on high-traffic surfaces) making adhesion primer especially critical when solvent test confirms alkyd base. Handrails and risers are highest-risk components for latex-over-oil delamination.

products.notes: Water-based for low VOC and easy cleanup. Bonds to glossy surfaces without full mechanical sanding. For SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: use only when adhesion test is marginal or existing sheen is semi-gloss+ or solvent test confirms alkyd base. For SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas, full prime if bare >30%. For SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime after complete scrape. Stair components are semi-gloss/gloss by default making adhesion primer more frequently required than on walls.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: conditional -- skip if adhesion test passes on low-sheen surfaces; apply if marginal adhesion or high-sheen existing finish or oil-based base identified via solvent test
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas (<30% bare) or full prime (>=30% bare)
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime -- extensive bare area after complete scrape

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Interior Stain-Blocking Primer (Shellac-Based)
material_systems.description: Shellac-based stain blocker for smoke-damaged stair components. Full-surface application required -- smoke contamination is pervasive even when not visually apparent. Baluster junctions, newel decorative detail, and handrail undersides trap concentrated smoke/nicotine deposits. Latex and acrylic primers have ZERO stain blocking capability (RC-002).

products.notes: Shellac is the ONLY product that reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. Full surface application required on all stair components. Strong odor -- requires ventilation (especially critical in enclosed stairwells). Fast dry (~45 min recoat). NOT water-cleanup -- requires denatured alcohol for tool cleaning. Turned baluster crevices and newel decorative details trap concentrated smoke deposits -- ensure full coverage of all profile details.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE: full surface -- mandatory, no exceptions. All 6 component types.

material_systems.cleanup: Denatured alcohol. Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. CON_DENATURED_ALCOHOL required.

material_systems.name: Interior Mildew-Resistant Primer
material_systems.description: Mildew-resistant primer with antimicrobial additives for moisture-damaged stair components. Applied after biocide treatment and full drying. Most common on basement stairwell stringers and risers where moisture wicks into wood, or stair systems adjacent to exterior doors. Gate condition: moisture SOURCE must be resolved before painting.

products.notes: Apply only after biocide treatment and full drying (24+ hrs). Contains antimicrobial additives preventing spore regrowth under paint film. Gate condition: active moisture source MUST be resolved by other trades. Basement stairwells and stairs near exterior doors are the most common application -- moisture enters at stringer-to-floor joint and wicks into end grain.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE: full surface prime on all affected areas -- mildew spores may be present beyond visible damage area

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: 100% acrylic enamel for standard residential stair repaint at QT3. Fast dry/recoat, non-yellowing, water cleanup. Good for enclosed stairwells where yellowing is a concern. Same product selection as NC stair, trim, and door specs. Non-yellowing is critical for enclosed stairwells with limited UV exposure.

example_products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss
products.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Standard production grade. Same product as NC stair finish at QT3. Non-yellowing property is especially valuable for enclosed stairwells with minimal UV exposure where alkyd products would yellow over time.

material_systems.notes: QT3 -- satin is the only sheen per sheen/QT gate. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Urethane-modified alkyd / waterbased alkyd for premium residential stair repaint at QT4. Superior flow and leveling, harder cured film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Sands easily between coats. Harder film resists scuffing on risers and hand-oil degradation on handrails.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane
products.notes: Superior flow and leveling. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Do not overwork. Sands easily between coats. Harder film than standard acrylic -- better scuff resistance on risers (toe-kick zone) and hand-oil resistance on handrails.

material_systems.notes: QT4. Semi-gloss is traditional/default stair sheen at this tier for durability. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Premium acrylic-urethane enamel for superior stair repaint at QT5. Maximum durability, excellent leveling, hardest film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Hardest film in the portfolio -- maximum scuff and hand-oil resistance for high-traffic stair surfaces.

products.coat_notes: QT5 brush typically requires 3 coats per FFD 15.10.3. QT5 spray: 2 coats standard.
products.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Hardest film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Sands easily between coats.

material_systems.notes: QT5. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion (RC-005).

material_systems.name: Polyurethane Topcoat for Handrails
material_systems.description: Optional water-based polyurethane clear topcoat applied over cured enamel finish on handrails ONLY at QT5. Provides maximum hand-oil resistance. In RP, even more valuable because existing handrails may have developed a patina of hand-oil absorption into the paint film -- the poly barrier prevents this on the fresh finish. Water-based poly to avoid yellowing over white/light colors.

example_products: General Finishes High Performance Water Based Topcoat
products.notes: Optional QT5 upgrade -- additional clear coat over enamel finish on handrails ONLY. Provides hand-oil resistance barrier. Water-based poly to avoid yellowing over white/light colors. Allow full enamel cure (24-48 hours) before poly application. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.1.

material_systems.notes: Optional. Handrails only. QT5 only. Additional clear coat for hand-oil resistance. Transfers DIRECT from NC railing spec.

ITM_STAIR_RISER.notes: Riser face ~2.2 SF per EA (3.5 ft wide x 0.625 ft high). Previously painted substrate absorbs less primer than bare wood. Higher coverage than NC bare-wood primer.

ITM_STAIR_STRINGER.notes: Stringer ~1 SF per LF (PDCA standard trim width). Open stringers may be 1.25 SF/LF due to notched profile.

ITM_STAIR_BALUSTER.notes: Square balusters ~1.5-2.0 SF/EA. Turned balusters ~2.0-3.0 SF/EA due to curved surface area. Profile type from PS_META.ENUM.BALUSTER_PROFILE.

ITM_STAIR_NEWEL.notes: Newel posts ~4-8 SF/EA depending on size and decorative detail. Midpoint 6 SF for material estimation.

ITM_STAIR_HANDRAIL.notes: Handrail: 4 paintable surfaces (top, 2 sides, underside) ~1.75 SF per LF.

ITM_STAIR_BASE_RAIL.notes: Base rail: 3 paintable surfaces ~0.875 SF per LF. Conditional item.

coverage_profiles.notes: Adhesion primer on previously painted stair surfaces. Lower porosity than bare wood results in higher coverage vs NC primer profiles (COV_STRS_PRIMER at 400 SF/gal). Coverage is consistent across primer types for this profile because all components are previously painted smooth surfaces.
assumptions: Previously painted substrate -- lower absorption than bare wood
Riser SF per unit ~2.2 SF (3.5 ft wide x 0.625 ft high)
Stringer ~1 SF per LF (PDCA standard trim width)
Baluster SF varies by profile (square < turned)
Handrail ~1.75 SF per LF (4-surface coverage)
Newel ~6 SF per EA (midpoint estimate)

coverage_profiles.notes: Shellac-based stain blocker has lower coverage than latex adhesion primer due to higher solids content and heavier required film build. Full surface application required on smoke-damaged stair components. Per-item SF equivalents are same as COV_STRP_PRIMER_ADHESION -- divide by 325 SF/gal instead of 425 SF/gal for material quantity. Turned baluster crevices and newel decorative details trap concentrated smoke deposits requiring additional material.
assumptions: Full surface application on smoke-damaged stair components
Shellac products have higher solids, lower spread rate than latex
Turned baluster profiles and newel decoration require additional material in crevices
Per-item SF equivalents same as adhesion primer profile

coverage_profiles.notes: Mildew-resistant primer coverage similar to adhesion primer -- latex-based formula. Slightly lower than adhesion due to thicker recommended film build for antimicrobial effectiveness. Typically applied to stringers and risers (moisture damage at stringer-to-floor junction in basement stairwells). Per-item SF equivalents same as COV_STRP_PRIMER_ADHESION.
assumptions: Latex formula -- similar coverage to adhesion primer
Slightly thicker film build for antimicrobial effectiveness
Stringers and risers are primary targets in basement stairwells
Per-item SF equivalents same as adhesion primer profile

ITM_STAIR_RISER.notes: Brush finish on riser face. Flat surface -- straightforward brush application.

ITM_STAIR_STRINGER.notes: Brush finish on stringer. Open stringers ~1.25 SF/LF -- use open_stringer_adjustment.

ITM_STAIR_BALUSTER.notes: Brush finish on balusters. Turned profiles have higher surface area AND material waste in crevices. Flow additive recommended for turned profiles to prevent roping.

ITM_STAIR_NEWEL.notes: Brush finish on newel posts. Decorative detail may reduce effective coverage.

ITM_STAIR_HANDRAIL.notes: Brush finish on handrail. 4 paintable surfaces. Thin coats on underside to prevent drips/sags.

ITM_STAIR_BASE_RAIL.notes: Brush finish on base rail. 3 paintable surfaces. Conditional item.

coverage_profiles.notes: Finish coat coverage for brush application on primed/prepared stair surfaces. Equivalent to NC fine-finish coverage because substrate condition after prime is equivalent. Coat count: QT3-QT4 = 2 coats, QT5 brush = 3 coats per FFD 15.10.3. Per-coat coverage is the same regardless of coat number.
assumptions: Primed smooth surface -- equivalent to NC after prime
Per-item SF equivalents from NC stair specs
Two-coat system standard; third coat at QT5 brush has same per-coat coverage
Flow additive usage does not significantly affect coverage rate

coverage_profiles.notes: Spray finish coverage rates use same base coverage as brush but add 20-30% material waste factor for overspray on complex stair geometry (balusters, newels, handrails with 4-surface access). Midpoint waste factor 1.25x (25% overspray). HVLP preferred over airless for in-place baluster work -- lower overspray. Per-item SF equivalents same as COV_STRP_FINISH_BRUSH. Effective material per gallon is reduced by waste factor.
assumptions: HVLP spray preferred (lower overspray than airless)
25% overspray waste on stair component geometry
Contained stairwell environment may increase overspray bounce-back
QT3-QT4 = 2 spray coats, QT5 spray = 2 spray coats

ITM_STAIR_HANDRAIL.notes: Poly topcoat on handrails only. Higher coverage than enamel due to thinner film build. One coat.

coverage_profiles.notes: Water-based polyurethane topcoat coverage on handrails. Higher coverage than enamel finish due to thinner recommended film build. Handrails only -- does not apply to other components. Transfers from NC railing spec.
assumptions: Cured enamel substrate -- no absorption
Single coat application
Handrail only -- 1.75 SF per LF

consumables.name: RP Assessment Kit (adhesion test + coating ID)
consumables.specification: Cross-hatch cutter, pressure-sensitive tape (ASTM D3359), mineral spirits, white rags for coating identification solvent test
consumables.notes: RP-specific assessment supplies. One kit per project. Includes ASTM D3359 cross-hatch adhesion test materials and solvent test supplies for latex vs oil-based coating identification. Stair components are HIGH RISK for oil-based existing paint -- coating ID is critical. Handrails and risers are especially likely to have alkyd coatings. Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: TSP (Trisodium Phosphate) Cleaner
consumables.specification: Powdered or liquid TSP concentrate, mixed per manufacturer directions
consumables.notes: RP stair-specific decontamination wash. Removes hand oils (concentrated on handrails and newels from daily use), cleaning chemical residue, and surface contaminants from existing paint before coating. Stair railings accumulate significant hand/body oil. One quart of concentrate makes enough solution for ~50 stair component cleaning passes. Not used in NC (new substrate is clean). Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Liquid Sander / Deglosser
consumables.specification: Liquid sander/deglosser for chemical degloss of existing paint, Krud Kutter Gloss-Off or equivalent
consumables.notes: RP-specific: chemical degloss for existing semi-gloss/gloss stair paint. Dulls existing sheen to promote adhesion without full mechanical sanding. Especially useful on turned balusters where mechanical sanding cannot reach all profile crevices -- chemical deglosser is faster and more thorough on complex profiles. One quart covers ~40 stair components (mixed EA/LF). Not used in NC. Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Flow Additive (Floetrol for latex / Penetrol for alkyd)
consumables.specification: Flow additive, Floetrol for waterborne products, Penetrol for alkyd-based products
consumables.notes: Extends working time 25-50%, improves leveling on turned balusters and handrails. Prevents roping on complex profiles. Floetrol for latex/acrylic, Penetrol for alkyd. One quart conditions approximately 4 quarts of finish. Critical for brush application on turned balusters. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.4. Transfers from NC railing spec.

consumables.name: Ram Board Stair Armor tread protector
consumables.specification: Ram Board Stair Armor with Spill Guard and grip strips, one per tread
consumables.notes: Mandatory tread protection from Day 1 through cleanup. Covers riser face bottom edge, tread surface, and bullnose. One per tread. NEVER use plastic sheeting on treads -- extreme fall hazard. In RP occupied context, tread walkability must be maintained throughout multi-day project. Daily integrity verification required. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2.

consumables.name: Low-tack safe-release masking tape
consumables.specification: Low-tack masking tape, safe for finished tread surfaces and carpet backing
consumables.notes: Secure tread protection (Stair Armor) without damaging finished tread surfaces. Also used for carpet runner protection attachment. Low-tack adhesive prevents damage during removal. 60 yards = 180 LF per roll.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 120-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 120 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: Aggressive grit for feathering scrape edges on failing/peeling stair components. Creates smooth transition from scraped to sound paint. Non-negotiable at all tiers -- feathering must be thorough on stairs (scrutinized surface). One sheet covers ~8 stair components for scrape edge feathering.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 150 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: General prep grit for degloss scuff sanding and mechanical surface preparation on sound paint. All tiers. One sheet per ~10 stair components for mechanical degloss. 150 grit for initial sanding of existing paint surfaces.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 180-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 180 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: Intermediate prep grit. Used for scuff sanding existing finish before primer application. Also suitable for primer scuff before finish coats. One sheet per ~10 stair components.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 220 grit, 9x11 inch

grit_by_tier.QT3: 220 -- spot sand nibs and rough spots only between coats
grit_by_tier.QT4: 220 -- full surface sand all components between coats

consumables.notes: Interstage sanding between finish coats and primer-to-finish sand. Spot sand at QT3, full surface at QT4. Rigid sanding block mandatory for flat surfaces (risers, stringer flats) per FFD 15.4.1. One sheet per ~10 stair components for interstage sanding.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 320 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: QT5 interstage sanding between finish coats. Thorough 220-320 grit sanding per FFD 15.10.3. Uniform scratch pattern required. One sheet per ~8 stair components (more thorough sanding at QT5). Rigid sanding block mandatory per FFD 15.4.1.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.specification: Rigid sanding block, fine grit range (150-220)
consumables.notes: Rigid blocks remove defects -- mandatory per FFD 15.4.1 for between-coat sanding on flat stair surfaces (riser faces, stringer flats, handrail top surface). Flexible sponges are NOT acceptable for defect leveling. One block per crew, reusable across coats.

consumables.name: Contour Sanding Sponge
consumables.specification: Flexible sanding sponge, medium/fine grit (150-220), angled edges for profile conformance
consumables.notes: Flexible sanding sponge for turned baluster profiles, newel decorative detail, and handrail contours where rigid blocks cannot reach. Conforms to curved profiles. Essential for turned balusters and ornate newel posts. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine: flexible sponges for profile-following only, NOT for defect leveling (use rigid block for flat surfaces). One sponge covers ~15 profiled components.

consumables.name: Scotch-Brite abrasive pad (180-220 grit equivalent)
consumables.specification: Scotch-Brite non-woven abrasive pad, 180-220 grit equivalent, green or maroon
consumables.notes: Conformable pad follows turned baluster contours and handrail profiles better than flat sandpaper. Excellent for degloss scuff sanding on complex profiles. Also suitable for primer scuff on profiled surfaces. One pad covers ~15 profiled components.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5 inch)
consumables.specification: 2-2.5 inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle (nylon/polyester blend)
consumables.notes: Primary brush for riser faces, stringer flat surfaces, handrail top/sides, and newel flat panels. One per painter per material type (primer brush + finish brush). Quality brush essential for smooth finish on stairs -- scrutinized surface.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (1.5 inch) for detail
consumables.specification: 1.5 inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle, for baluster junction and detail work
consumables.notes: Smaller detail brush for riser edges, stringer profiles, baluster-to-tread junctions, baluster-to-handrail junctions, and newel decorative detail. One per material type.

consumables.name: German Round Trim Brush (1.25 inch)
consumables.specification: 1.25 inch German round trim brush, natural or synthetic bristle
consumables.notes: Purpose-made for turned/ornate baluster complex profiles. Round profile follows turned baluster contours. Significantly reduces roping on complex profiles. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 12.1. One per material type when turned balusters are in scope. Transfers from NC railing spec.

consumables.name: Brush for shellac (dedicated)
consumables.specification: 2-inch angled sash brush, dedicated for shellac use, natural or synthetic bristle
consumables.notes: Dedicated brush for shellac stain-blocking primer (BIN). Shellac requires alcohol cleanup -- keep separate from latex brushes. Conditional on smoke damage substrate state. One per project.

consumables.name: Airless spray tip 310-411 or HVLP nozzle
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 310-411 range (6-8 inch fan, 0.010-0.011 orifice) or HVLP fine-finish nozzle
consumables.notes: Fine atomization for stair component spray finish. HVLP preferred over airless for in-place baluster work (less overspray in enclosed stairwell). If airless: fine-finish tips (Graco FFLP 108, 210/310 series, 4-6 inch fan). Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.3. One tip per ~50 components.

consumables.name: Spray gun filter
consumables.specification: In-line filter for airless spray gun or HVLP gun cup filter
consumables.notes: Replace when clogged or every ~50 gallons. One per spray setup.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.specification: Resin-impregnated cheesecloth for dust removal
consumables.notes: Wipe stair component surfaces immediately before each coat application to remove sanding dust. Essential for quality finish per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.12. One tack cloth covers ~20 stair components (mixed EA/LF units). Use before every coat for dust-free surface.

consumables.name: Blue painter's tape 1.5-inch
consumables.specification: Blue painter's tape, 1.5-inch width, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: Wall masking along stringer edge, riser-to-tread edge masking, baluster junction taping (when taping technique used), spray containment taping. Usage: brush ~2-3 LF per riser for edge masking; spray ~20+ LF per flight for wall masking. 60 yards = 180 LF per roll.

consumables.name: Tape & Drape Film (pre-taped masking film)
consumables.specification: Pre-taped masking film, 24-48 inch width, for wall/surface spray containment
consumables.notes: Spray containment on walls adjacent to railing system. Faster application than separate tape + plastic sheeting. Applied behind baluster runs and along stairwell walls during spray application. 20 yards = ~65 LF per roll.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.specification: Canvas drop cloth, 4x12 ft runner or 4x5 ft compact
consumables.notes: Floor protection at landing areas (top and bottom of stairway). Runner-style for landings. In RP, landing floors are almost always finished (unlike NC where subfloor is common). 1-2 per stairway system, reusable.

consumables.name: Rosin paper (red or brown)
consumables.specification: Rosin paper roll, 36-inch width, 500 SF per roll
consumables.notes: Carpet runner protection -- rosin paper over carpet edges at paint work zones. Also usable as supplemental tread protection layer under Stair Armor for premium protection. In RP occupied homes, carpet runners on stairs are common. Not present in NC (carpet installed after painting).

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.specification: Paintable acrylic latex caulk, white, 10.1 oz tube
consumables.notes: Stringer-to-wall caulk joint assess/replace and riser-to-stringer joint assess/replace. RP caulk replacement is selective -- assess each joint, replace only deteriorated sections (typically 15-30% of total joint length). Newel-to-tread and newel-to-handrail junction caulk assess/replace. One tube covers approximately 25 LF of caulk joint. Allow cure time before coating.

consumables.name: Caulk gun
consumables.specification: Standard caulk gun, ratchet-type
consumables.notes: Reusable tool for caulk application. One per crew.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackling compound
consumables.specification: Lightweight spackling compound, tub or squeeze tube
consumables.notes: For patching scrape edges, filling gouges, and repairing defects revealed after degloss/scrape on RP stair components. GOOD condition typically has no fill work. FAIR/POOR condition: fill scraped transition areas, surface defects, and small dents on risers, stringers, newels. One quart per ~30 stair components at FAIR condition.

consumables.name: Sandable wood filler
consumables.specification: Sandable wood filler, lightweight or auto-body type depending on defect depth
consumables.notes: For filling deeper defects, fastener holes, and impact damage on stair components. Auto-body type for deep fills, lightweight for shallow. One quart per ~50 stair components. Used alongside CON_FILLER_LIGHTWEIGHT for different defect depths.

consumables.name: Flexible putty knife
consumables.specification: Flexible putty knife, 1.5-inch or 2-inch
consumables.notes: For applying filler/spackle to defects and scrape edges. Flexible blade for flush fill on flat stair surfaces. One per crew, reusable.

consumables.name: Solvent cleaner for metal prep
consumables.specification: Mineral spirits or equivalent for SSPC-SP 1 solvent cleaning
consumables.notes: For iron balusters in RP that require re-priming. SSPC-SP 1 solvent wipe removes manufacturing oils and hand-oil buildup. Conditional on iron balusters with failing powder coat or paint. One quart covers ~100 balusters. Transfers from NC railing spec.

consumables.name: Denatured alcohol
consumables.specification: Denatured alcohol for shellac cleanup
consumables.notes: Required for cleaning brushes and tools used with shellac stain-blocking primer (BIN). Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. One quart per project. Conditional on smoke damage substrate state.

stair_tread_covers.description: Mandatory tread protection from Day 1 through cleanup. FIRST setup task, LAST teardown task.
stair_tread_covers.condition: ALWAYS -- mandatory regardless of method or tier. In RP occupied context, daily verification of protection integrity required. NEVER use plastic sheeting on treads -- extreme fall hazard. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2.

floor_perimeter.description: Drop cloth runners at landing areas (top and bottom of stairway)
floor_perimeter.condition: Almost always in RP -- landing floors are finished in occupied homes.

wall_adjacent.description: Wall masking along stringer edge and railing area
wall_adjacent.condition: Required for spray method. In RP, may also be needed for brush method near finished walls at stringer-to-wall junction.

spray_containment.description: Cardboard shields behind balusters, Tape & Drape on walls for spray containment
spray_containment.condition: Spray method only. HVLP preferred over airless for in-place baluster work. 45+ min setup for typical 39-62 baluster system.

carpet_runner_protection.description: Rosin paper over carpet runner edges at paint work zones
carpet_runner_protection.condition: RP-specific: occupied homes with carpet runners on stairs. Not present in NC (carpet installed after painting). Rosin paper protects carpet edges where paint work occurs.

Stringer LF for material quantity calculation
Baluster count for material quantity calculation
Newel post count for material quantity calculation
Handrail LF for material quantity and optional poly topcoat calculation
Base rail LF for material quantity calculation
Stringer-to-wall caulk LF -- RP assess/replace (15-30% typical replacement)
Wall masking LF (spray method or brush near finished walls)

compatibility_rules.description: Adhesion primer under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Water-based adhesion primer is compatible with all fine-finish topcoat chemistries. Scuff sand primer before finish coats.

compatibility_rules.description: Shellac stain blocker under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac seals stains and is compatible with all topcoat chemistries. Universal undercoat.

compatibility_rules.description: Mildew primer under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Latex-based mildew primer is compatible with all fine-finish topcoat chemistries.

compatibility_rules.description: No primer skip for sound paint with latex existing coating and passing adhesion test
compatibility_rules.notes: GOOD condition with verified latex-over-latex compatibility. No primer needed -- proceed directly to finish coats after degloss. Most common residential stair RP scenario.

compatibility_rules.description: Adhesion primer REQUIRED when existing coating is alkyd regardless of condition
compatibility_rules.notes: Stair components historically received oil-based paint. Latex over un-primed alkyd coating WILL delaminate. Adhesion primer is non-negotiable when solvent test confirms alkyd. This is the primary adhesion failure mode on stair RP. Handrails are highest risk -- constant hand contact stresses the paint film.

compatibility_rules.description: Shellac BIN is sole primer for smoke damage -- no adhesion primer substitution
compatibility_rules.notes: Latex and acrylic primers have ZERO stain blocking capability (RC-002). Shellac is the ONLY product that reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. No adhesion primer substitution allowed for smoke damage.

compatibility_rules.description: Sheen/QT gate enforcement for stair components
compatibility_rules.notes: Satin at QT3+. Semi-gloss at QT4+ (default for stairs -- toe-kick scuff resistance on risers, hand-oil resistance on handrails). Gloss at QT5 only. Flat/matte/eggshell NOT valid for stairs per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 7.2.
Water-based poly over cured enamel. Allow full enamel cure (24-48 hours) before poly application. QT5 only. Handrails only -- does not apply to balusters, newels, risers, stringers, or base rails.

compatibility_rules.description: Baluster profile affects coverage rates but not product compatibility
compatibility_rules.notes: Turned balusters have higher SF per unit (2.5 vs 1.75 SF/EA) consuming more material per unit. Profile does NOT affect product compatibility -- same systems apply to both profiles. Flow additive (CON_FLOW_ADDITIVE) recommended for turned profiles to prevent roping.

compatibility_rules.description: Modified urethane finish over deglossed/primed existing stair coating
compatibility_rules.notes: Modified urethane finish coats adhere well to deglossed/primed existing coatings. SHORT working time -- critical on complex stair geometry (apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1). Do not overwork on turned balusters or handrail undersides.

compatibility_rules.description: Handrail blocking resistance -- higher sheen and harder film preferred
compatibility_rules.notes: Handrails are touched daily -- maximum blocking resistance is critical. Semi-gloss or gloss preferred over satin for hand-oil resistance. QT4+ (modified urethane) has harder film than QT3 (standard acrylic). QT5 optional poly topcoat provides additional hand-oil barrier.

risk_notes.topic: Latex over alkyd delamination on stair components
risk_notes.risk: Interior stair components historically received oil-based paint. Latex applied directly over hard, glossy alkyd surface without adhesion primer will delaminate. Handrails and risers are highest risk due to daily physical contact.
risk_notes.mitigation: Coating identification (solvent test) in assessment phase is MANDATORY. Adhesion primer required when alkyd existing coating detected. Never skip primer over oil-based existing paint.

risk_notes.topic: Tread damage from drips/spills during stair component painting
risk_notes.risk: Drips, spills, or foot traffic damage on unprotected treads during multi-day RP project in occupied home
risk_notes.mitigation: Ram Board Stair Armor from Day 1 -- FIRST setup task. NEVER plastic sheeting on treads (fall hazard). Daily integrity verification in RP occupied context. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2.

risk_notes.topic: Fall hazard from improper tread protection
risk_notes.risk: Plastic sheeting used on treads instead of non-slip Stair Armor
risk_notes.mitigation: Doctrine MANDATES Ram Board Stair Armor or equivalent non-slip protection. NEVER plastic sheeting. Preventable with proper specification.

risk_notes.risk: Fast-drying waterborne product creates visible brush marks (roping) on complex turned profiles
risk_notes.mitigation: Flow additive (CON_FLOW_ADDITIVE -- Floetrol for latex, Penetrol for alkyd). German round trim brushes (CON_BRUSH_ROUND_TRIM) for turned profiles. Thin coats. Per Stairway_Systems_Doctrine Section 12.1.

risk_notes.risk: Excessive film build on handrail underside causes runs and sags -- highly visible defect
risk_notes.mitigation: Thin coats, proper flow additive. QT4+ remove brackets and paint handrails horizontally if possible. Check for drips during flash time.

risk_notes.topic: Adhesion failure on previously scraped areas
risk_notes.risk: Feathered edges not properly sanded smooth before priming causes visible transition lines and localized adhesion failure
risk_notes.mitigation: Feather sand all scraped edges to smooth transition with 120 grit. Adhesion primer over entire scraped area. Sand primer before finish coat.

risk_notes.topic: Mildew recurrence after painting over moisture damage
risk_notes.risk: Moisture source not resolved before painting -- mildew returns under paint film
risk_notes.mitigation: Moisture meter check in assessment. Gate condition: moisture source MUST be resolved by other trades before painting. Biocide treatment + SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT. Rare on stairs but possible in basement stairwells.

risk_notes.topic: Lead paint on pre-1978 stair components
risk_notes.risk: Stair components are HIGH RISK for lead paint -- historically oil-based, typically multi-layer from multiple repaints. Scraping/sanding generates lead-containing dust.
risk_notes.mitigation: MOD_RRP_INT_CONTAINMENT conditional on PS_META.BOOL.HOME_PRE_1978. RRP-certified renovator required. Containment, HEPA vacuum, and wet methods per EPA RRP Rule.

risk_notes.risk: Shellac/BIN primer and solvent-based products concentrate fumes in enclosed stairwells -- occupant health risk in occupied homes
risk_notes.mitigation: Ventilation is mandatory during and after shellac application. Portable fans at top and bottom of stairwell. Schedule shellac application when occupants can vacate. Water-based finish coats reduce ongoing VOC exposure.

material_notes.selection_guidance: Material system selection: PRIMER is state-driven (adhesion for sound/failing/peeling with alkyd base, stain-block for smoke, mildew for moisture). FINISH is QT-driven per Fine Finish Doctrine: QT3 = SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, QT4 = SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, QT5 = SYS_FF_PREMIUM. All 6 component types use the same finish system. Optional poly topcoat on handrails at QT5.
material_notes.dual_system_architecture: TWO independent material system layers: (1) Primer systems are STATE-DRIVEN with 3 RP systems (adhesion, stain-block, mildew) plus no-primer path. (2) Finish systems are QT-driven with 3 tiers. Any primer can pair with any finish. Optional poly topcoat at QT5 for handrails. This replaces the NC substrate-driven primer architecture (8+ NC primer systems reduced to 3 RP state-driven systems).
material_notes.nc_to_rp_primer_mapping: NC had 8+ substrate-specific primer systems (MDF shellac, MDF latex, poplar stain-block, hardwood tannin-block, plywood sealer, iron DTM, powder coat bonding, standard wood). RP replaces ALL with 3 state-driven systems because substrate is already coated from original NC work. Iron balusters with failing powder coat are a special case -- may need bonding primer, addressed within adhesion primer scope.
material_notes.coverage_variability: Coverage varies significantly by component type due to SF-per-unit differences: risers ~2.2 SF/EA, balusters square ~1.75 SF/EA, balusters turned ~2.5 SF/EA, newels ~6 SF/EA, stringers ~1 SF/LF, handrails ~1.75 SF/LF, base rails ~0.875 SF/LF. Material quantity calculation must account for mixed UOM across the 6 item types.
material_notes.rp_vs_nc_differences: RP uses state-driven RP primers instead of NC substrate-driven primers. RP primer coverage is higher than NC because previously painted surfaces absorb less (425 SF/gal vs NC 400 SF/gal). RP adds TSP wash, liquid deglosser, assessment kit, contour sanding sponges, and Tape & Drape not needed in NC. RP reuses from NC: flow additive, German round brush, Stair Armor, all finish systems, poly topcoat.
material_notes.open_time_by_chemistry: Standard acrylic enamel has moderate open time. Modified urethane/waterborne alkyd (Advance, Emerald Urethane) has SHORT open time (5-10 min) -- do not overwork per FFD 15.3.1. SHORT working time is especially challenging on turned balusters -- flow additive is critical.
material_notes.coat_count_summary: QT3-QT4: 2 finish coats standard. QT5 brush: 3 finish coats per FFD 15.10.3. QT5 spray: 2 finish coats. Prime coat (when applicable) is always 1 coat. Poly topcoat (when applicable) is always 1 coat.
material_notes.product_classification: Advance is waterborne alkyd. Emerald Urethane is acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Both have SHORT working times.

assumptions.value: RP adhesion primer at 425 SF/gal vs NC bare-wood primer at 400 SF/gal
assumptions.source: Previously painted surfaces absorb less primer than bare wood. Aligned with SF_DOOR_INT_RP adhesion primer coverage (425 SF/gal).
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines RP vs NC primer coverage differential. Derived from product PDS typical coverage range and field practice.

assumptions.value: ~2.2 SF per riser (3.5 ft wide x 0.625 ft high)
Square ~1.5-2.0 SF, Turned ~2.0-3.0 SF per baluster
assumptions.source: Estimated from typical baluster dimensions (34-36 inch height, 1.25-1.75 inch profile). Aligned with SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC.

assumptions.value: ~1.75 SF per LF (4-surface coverage: top, 2 sides, underside)
assumptions.source: Estimated from typical handrail profile (~2.5 inch width x 3 inch height). Aligned with SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC.

assumptions.value: ~4-8 SF per EA depending on size and decorative detail. Midpoint 6 SF.
assumptions.source: Estimated from typical newel post dimensions. Aligned with SF_STAIR_RAILING_NC.

assumptions.value: 25% overspray waste on stair component geometry (1.25x material factor)
assumptions.source: NC stair specs note 20-30% spray waste for overspray in confined stairwell space. HVLP reduces waste vs airless.

assumptions.value: 1 quart concentrate per ~50 stair component cleaning passes
assumptions.source: Field practice estimate. Higher yield than door RP (30 per quart) because stair components are smaller per unit than door openings.
